jobs.prompt: T-0178: write docs/ops/cluster-ledger-cutover.md, a runbook for migrating the Mac mini + MacBook from two independent local ticket ledgers to one shared cluster ledger (the T-0175/T-0176/T-0177 work, read all three as context: tools/cluster-ledger-api.mjs is the canonical-side HTTP listener and HMAC auth, tools/cluster-client.mjs is the follower-side client with its own fail-closed/timeout/redirect/host-validation behavior, tools/ledger-merge.mjs is the one-time ledger-merge tool used to combine the two machines' existing tickets.json/security-reviews/journal into one before cutover). The doc needs three sections matching the ticket's acceptance exactly: (1) Which machine is canonical, how to configure the follower, and the exact command sequence - name one machine as canonical (the one that will run `remoteClusterMode: true` and host the listener on `clusterLedgerPort`, default 9448, bound to 127.0.0.1 and exposed over the tailnet via `tailscale serve` per the existing code comment - do not invent a different exposure mechanism), name the other as follower (sets `clusterCanonicalHost` in its local config, per tools/cluster-client.mjs's `resolveClusterCanonicalHost`), and the manual node-registry provisioning step this already requires (per the T-0175/T-0176 handoff notes: there is no registration endpoint yet, so each node's id+secret entry in `~/.project-swarm/nodes/registry.json` - or `SWARM_NODES_REGISTRY_FILE`/`SWARM_HOME` override - must be copied onto the canonical machine out of band, e.g. scp over the tailnet, never committed or emailed in plaintext). Give the exact sequence: run tools/ledger-merge.mjs in dry-run first (report-only, default), review the collision/merge report, only then run it with `apply:true` to write the merged ledger; start the canonical listener; provision the follower's node secret into the canonical registry; set `clusterCanonicalHost` on the follower; verify with a real `swarm queue claim`/`release` round-trip from the follower before relying on it. (2) Rollback: what to do if the remote API becomes unreachable from the follower - since tools/cluster-client.mjs fails closed (it throws rather than silently falling back), a follower that needs to keep working during an outage must be explicitly reconfigured back to local-only (unset `clusterCanonicalHost`/`remoteClusterMode`) rather than relying on an automatic fallback that does not exist; include manual reconcile instructions for merging back any claims/releases that happened locally on either machine during the outage once the remote API is restored (reuse tools/ledger-merge.mjs's dry-run-first/collision-is-a-hard-error pattern for this reconcile too, since it is the same two-ledgers-into-one problem). (3) Disabling legacy hand-off branches: a step confirming both machines are healthy on the shared ledger (both can claim/release through the remote API without error) before the old manual hand-off-branch workflow (coordination/HANDOFF.md-driven manual coordination between machines) is turned off, so there is no window where neither mechanism is authoritative. Keep the whole doc concrete and runnable (actual flag names, file paths, and command lines from the real code, not generic placeholders) - do not invent config keys, endpoints, or commands that don't exist in the context files.
